payload.query: Summarise UPI OC 186A in a short overview and key requirements.

claims.text: UPI Operating Circular 186A introduces UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS) terminals as an additional mode for initiating contactless NFC-based UPI payments.
This enhancement extends the existing UPI Tap & Pay via QR functionality to allow users to make payments by unlocking their mobile device and tapping it on a PoS terminal.
UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Payee PSPs must enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
UPI Application Providers and PSP Banks must obtain explicit user consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Members and UPI Application Providers must obtain explicit user consent for enabling the UPI Tap & Pay feature, with users having the ability to opt out at any time.
Payee PSPs are required to integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) on all PoS terminals under their acquiring network.
UPI Application Providers must ensure device lock is enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.
The per transaction limit for UPI Tap & Pay is capped at INR 5000, up to which additional factor of authentication shall not be required.
UPI Application Providers must make UPI Tap & Pay available through a dedicated call-to-action as a standalone feature, not embedded within other services or menus.
Settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution for UPI Tap & Pay transactions must be carried out in accordance with extant UPI guidelines.
Members shall follow RBI guidelines on Harmonization of Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation for failed transactions using authorized Payment Systems.
Members and UPI Application Providers must refer to the applicable UPI Tap & Pay Feature Document, Technical Specifications, and other instructions issued by NPCI for detailed requirements.

claims.text: UPI Operating Circular 186 introduces UPI Tap & Pay as a new mode for transactions in addition to existing modes like Scan & Pay and Pay to Contact.
Circular 186 specifies that UPI Tap & Pay is available only on mobile devices having NFC capability.
Circular 186 requires UPI APPs to take permission from the customer to enable NFC for Tap & Pay transactions.
Under Circular 186, a transaction amount of Rs.500 or less on Tap is processed through UPI LITE account if enabled by the user, otherwise with UPI PIN.
Circular 186 states that transactions exceeding Rs.500 on Tap require a UPI PIN and are processed online.
Circular 186 mandates the use of initiation mode '06' for all UPI Tap & Pay transactions.
Circular 186 requires acquiring banks to ensure NFC tags used in UPI Smart QRs are NFC forum certified (Type 2) and non-rewritable post personalisation.
Circular 186 directs acquiring banks to procure NFC Tags from NPCI empanelled vendors as communicated via specific circulars.
Circular 186 sets a go-live date for the UPI Tap & Pay functionality by 31st January 2024.
UPI Operating Circular 186A enhances UPI Tap & Pay by extending it to Point of Sale (PoS) terminals for contactless NFC-based payments.
Circular 186A restricts UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions only.
Circular 186A requires Payee PSPs to enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
Circular 186A mandates that Remitter Banks validate the User's account for UPI Tap & Pay feature enablement status before processing each transaction.
Circular 186A allows Users to set their own transaction limits within a ceiling of Rs.5000.
Circular 186A requires explicit User consent after each device binding operation before allowing further UPI Tap & Pay transactions.
Circular 186A ensures Users have the ability to opt out of the UPI Tap & Pay feature at any time.
Circular 186A requires Payee PSPs to integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) on all PoS terminals under their acquiring network.
Circular 186A mandates that device lock is enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be unlocked during transaction initiation.
Circular 186A caps the per transaction limit at Rs.5000, up to which additional factor of authentication is not required.
Circular 186A requires UPI Tap & Pay to be presented as a standalone feature and not embedded within other services or menu categories.
Circular 186A states that settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution for UPI Tap & Pay transactions follow extant UPI guidelines.

claims.text: UPI Operating Circular 186 introduces UPI Tap & Pay as a new mode for transactions in addition to existing modes like Scan & Pay and Pay to Contact.
Circular 186 specifies that UPI Tap & Pay is available only on mobile devices having NFC capability.
Circular 186 requires UPI APPs to take permission from the customer to enable NFC for Tap & Pay transactions.
Under Circular 186, a transaction amount of Rs.500 or less on Tap is processed through UPI LITE account if enabled by the user, otherwise with UPI PIN.
Circular 186 states that transactions exceeding Rs.500 on Tap require a UPI PIN and are processed online.
Circular 186 mandates the use of initiation mode '06' for all UPI Tap & Pay transactions.
Circular 186 requires acquiring banks to ensure NFC tags used in UPI Smart QRs are NFC forum certified (Type 2) and non-rewritable post personalisation.
Circular 186 directs acquiring banks to procure NFC Tags from NPCI empanelled vendors as communicated via specific circulars.
Circular 186 sets a go-live date for the UPI Tap & Pay functionality by 31st January 2024.
UPI Operating Circular 186A enhances UPI Tap & Pay by extending it to Point of Sale (PoS) terminals for contactless NFC-based payments.
Circular 186A restricts UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions only.
Circular 186A requires Payee PSPs to enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
Circular 186A mandates that Remitter Banks validate the User's account for UPI Tap & Pay feature enablement status before processing each transaction.
Circular 186A allows Users to set their own transaction limits within a ceiling of Rs.5000.
Circular 186A requires explicit User consent after each device binding operation before allowing further UPI Tap & Pay transactions.
Circular 186A ensures Users have the ability to opt out of the UPI Tap & Pay feature at any time.
Circular 186A requires Payee PSPs to integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) on all PoS terminals under their acquiring network.
Circular 186A mandates that device lock is enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be unlocked during transaction initiation.
Circular 186A caps the per transaction limit at Rs.5000, up to which additional factor of authentication is not required.
Circular 186A requires UPI Tap & Pay to be presented as a standalone feature and not embedded within other services or menu categories.
Circular 186A states that settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution for UPI Tap & Pay transactions follow extant UPI guidelines.
